quest.title: Calamitous Tread
quest.description: Just as everything seems to have returned to normal, an unknown catastrophe arrives suddenly, like a thief in the night...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x950, Mora x41750, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're back!

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Welcome back. Do you want a cup of tea?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How can you be so much like Wriothesley, always drinking tea...

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Huh, actually, now that you mention it, I just remembered something now.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: While I was sedated, I could still barely hear two people talking next to me. They were discussing everything from the leaves to the water and even the teacups themselves...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: ...Must have been Wriothesley and Sigewinne.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Yeah, I heard one male voice and one female, so it should have been the two of them. They... really were just talking about brewing tea.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: I really can't make sense of this place...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: #So, {NICKNAME}, Paimon... Were you able to learn anything from Wriothesley?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, he explained everything.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Very well... then would you mind checking your answers against my speculations?

choices.text: Lyney sounds a lot more like his old self.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Yeah, I took the time to rest, so I'm feeling a lot more relaxed now.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: ...Nobody else is around, and Miss Sigewinne is also busy with something or other, so let's just talk here.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Alright. Then, I'll posit my theories. I asked myself three questions.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Firstly, why was Freminet affected by the Primordial Seawater? It was because he dove into the sea. My theory is... the long lost Primordial Sea is probably very close to the Fortress of Meropide.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, he's good! He got that right on the first try!

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: That's our Lyney.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Secondly, Wriothesley's attitude changed dramatically during the course of our stay here. He ignored us completely at first, then suddenly roadblocked us. Why?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I spent quite a long time thinking about this. If he has been monitoring the Fatui since the very beginning, he probably ignored us at first because he was hoping we could find Master Childe for him.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: What's more, the Fortress of Meropide is not a part of Fontaine's court system, nor does it report to Iudex Neuvillette. Wriothesley is basically the king of a no man's land.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: As long as the Fortress doesn't do anything about Master Childe's disappearance, "Father" can use it to pressure the Fontaine authorities. And while the two factions are pitted against each other, Wriothesley will be free to move between the parties of interest.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: If I had to guess, he probably has something that he's working on himself. It's likely related to the secret of the infirmary, but I just can't think of what it could be...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Lyney's grasp of the big picture is amazing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're super smart!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Haha, thanks so much. Then finally, there's the last question.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: If Wriothesley does have a plan, what could it be? All I know for now is that his plan probably has something to do with the changing nature of the seawater. He's even gotten Clorinde to help him out...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: ...That can't be the full extent of what he's doing. There's probably a secret passageway behind the block in the infirmary, and there's something big in the Fortress that most people here never get to see. He has a bargaining chip, and it could be important enough for "Father" to deal with him directly.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I don't have enough information, so I have no idea what his chip might be. But let me guess... you have the last piece of the puzzle.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After some deliberation, you share the information you just learned with Lyney and company.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: While sharing what you saw, you emphasize that now is not the time for disputes, and it's very important that they take the matter seriously and considerately.

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: I can't believe it...

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: The sea... will engulf everyone. Just like the prophecy said...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Could Wriothesley have wanted to meet "Father" to figure out a way to deal with this crisis?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: If you remember, I once mentioned that "Father" sees the House of the Hearth as her base of operations, and she truly wants to resolve the crisis. But how could Wriothesley have known that?

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Or perhaps, he didn't know, and just wanted to bring "Father" over to his side? Which could be why he said he just wanted to "negotiate."

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: #...Yeah, that makes sense to me. I understand your concerns as well, {NICKNAME}. I'll figure out a way to pass this on to our "Father." No matter what, we're on your side.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: The two of you have already aided us far too much. We probably would not be standing here right now if not for you.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: If you ever need anything else going forward, please come to the House of the Hearth at any time.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Though you may not share the sentiment, after all that we've gone through together, the three of us basically see you as family now.

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: ...You have my gratitude.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Thank you for protecting Lyney when it really mattered, and thank you for sharing the secrets of the Fortress with us. We didn't think you were going to do it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why are you being so formal all of a sudden?

choices.text: Don't mention it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *growl*...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What was that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah... Paimon... Paimon's hungry...

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: You've done so much already, go get some food!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, then we'll catch you guys another time!

choices.text: We can work together again if necessary.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Given your strength, you might not need our help at all. But if you are ever in danger, we will try our best to protect you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aww! The sound of that makes Paimon feel all warm and safe inside!

choices.text: Feeling better now, Lyney?

dialogues.speaker: Prison Broadcast
dialogues.text: It's time for dinner. Welfare Meals now being served in the Coupon Cafeteria!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Come on, let's go pick up ours as well!

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: #Ah, {NICKNAME} and Paimon! Over here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you here for dinner too, Miss Sigewinne?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Mhm, and I'm taking the opportunity to prepare Miss Clorinde's dinner as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, you're right... She's actually sitting in the fortress cafeteria...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: What would you like to eat?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh? We can choose?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Yep, you can! I've already talked to our chef, Mr. Wolsey. It's all on me today, so you can get whatever you'd like.

choices.text: Then I'll have the tastiest stuff you have to offer!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Me too, don't forget Paimon!

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: No problem! Just leave it to me.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After a while, the meals Sigewinne ordered for you arrive. Unlike days prior when you had to rely solely on luck, the dishes before you today are bursting with flavor.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Sigewinne also brings some drinks over to you. They taste a little strange, but she insists that they are very nutritious... She also insists that Wriothesley is also a fan of them, but neither you nor Paimon buy her claims.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: ...Okay, the shakes genuinely taste pretty terrible. At the very least, however, they help you to calm down and relax.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahhhh!! Sooo delicious!!

choices.text: Amazing!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's so happy, Paimon wants to feast like this every day, hehe.

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Feeling full yet? How's the food?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Delicious!

choices.text: Exquisite, thank you!

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Aw, I'm so glad to see you all so happy! See, the expression on your face just now... The muscle here just moved, which suggests that you're feeling quite relaxed at the moment.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sigewinne, do you do this to help your patients, or to better understand human beings?

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: A bit of both, I suppose. I'm a Melusine, which means I'm very different from human beings. I must know what you're thinking if I want to take good care of you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're really good at taking care of people... Even though you're so short, you still talk and act like an older sister.

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Really? You're reminded of an older sister? Hehe, that's great to hear.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, and what did you mean back in Wriothesley's office, when you said that you were protecting Lyney and his siblings as well?

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Oh, that? I just asked His Grace to look out for those children, especially that diver boy. I was getting a bit worried after hearing that something was wrong with the water...

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Thankfully, Clorinde is very strong, and managed to save him in the nick of time. His Grace also sealed the pipes after Clorinde left to make sure that Lyney wouldn't impulsively chase after his brother.

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Although the path was blocked, we still stationed some guards there to stop anyone from approaching. They were instructed to only open the door once Miss Clorinde had returned.

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Oh, and I was keeping an eye on Mr. Lyney as well. We had to press him, but we couldn't allow him to be in any real danger.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You are all super considerate and really thought everything through...

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Hehe, it's just what we do down here at the Fortress. At least, this has been His Grace's style for as long as he's been the leader.

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: *sigh* I really wish Monsieur Neuvillette would come down here more often too. I feel like he'd like it here... With all the darkness and chaos...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (But that doesn't make sense at all... It's hard to imagine Neuvillette outside of his office...)

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Get a good night's rest, you two! You've both worked very hard.

choices.text: Besides the milk— Uh, I mean, everything was super delicious!
Free dinners are the absolute best!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is this how it feels to be freeloaders? Wait a second, we did do plenty of work, after all...

choices.text: Then I'll get the biggest portion you have to offer!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Clorinde!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you two.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How's dinner?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: It's alright. Miss Sigewinne really put in a lot of effort.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So we heard that Wriothesley invited you to come down to help and you saved Freminet, too. You sure work super fast.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: It was child's play.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, Paimon didn't know even Champion Duelists could take on side jobs...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh and, why aren't you eating with Sigewinne and the Duke? Won't you get bored eating by yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Miss Sigewinne was with you, and the Duke has business of his own.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hm... Actually, didn't Navia say that you went out for dinner with her as well?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Yeah. First time in a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "First time in a long time"? So you mean, you've gone out to dinner with her in the past?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: In the past, yes.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: You seem to be enjoying yourselves here.

choices.text: It's all thanks to Neuvillette...

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Things will be getting messy at the Fortress soon. Don't run around unnecessarily.

choices.text: This is technically a work trip for us too...

talks.objective: Return to the dormitories to rest

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... So much has happened, Paimon just feels absolutely exhausted now that she's finally relaxed...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's super sleepy... Are you sleepy, too...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, I'm also getting there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Zzz... Zzz...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Wow, she really immediately fell asleep.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Delicious... Paimon wants seconds... For free!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Goodnight.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happened, why is everyone running around... Hey! What are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Hurried Prisoner
dialogues.text: No time to explain, mate! Goodbye!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Hey, wait!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's wrong with these people!? They won't even talk to us!

dialogues.speaker: Cuistot
dialogues.text: They're here! Ah, there you are!

dialogues.speaker: Laverune
dialogues.text: Thank goodness.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cuistot and Laverune? Do you know what happened here?

dialogues.speaker: Cuistot
dialogues.text: We came here especially to inform you! Something seems to have gone terribly wrong just now, His Grace is telling everyone to evacuate and get out of here.

dialogues.speaker: Cuistot
dialogues.text: Laverune was saying, you two are new here, and don't have many friends, so you might slip through the cracks. Haven't you heard of stories like that? An evacuation is successfully completed, yet you only find out once you do a headcount that one or two people are missing...

dialogues.speaker: Laverune
dialogues.text: Wait, weren't you the one who brought that up? Why is it suddenly my idea?

dialogues.speaker: Cuistot
dialogues.text: Hey, shut up!

dialogues.speaker: Laverune
dialogues.text: Okay, whatever. The point is, you should come with us.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You said His Grace said to... evacuate "outwards"?

dialogues.speaker: Laverune
dialogues.text: Yeah, he said to get as far away as possible, upwards and outwards.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Then that means whatever happened must have happened down below... Oh no, isn't that gate at the very bottom!?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, it can't be that thing!

dialogues.speaker: Cuistot
dialogues.text: What? Hey! Where are you going!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We have to go find the Duke! You two, just go and get out! Go on without us!

dialogues.speaker: Laverune
dialogues.text: Hey! Heyyy! ...Be careful!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Alright. Seems like the problem inside has been suppressed.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Let me guess, we're safe for now?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Indeed, but only for now.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I win this bet. You owe me a present.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Very well, it was indeed just as you said.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: You made a bet?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: We made a bet on the size of your entourage. Clorinde thought you wouldn't come down by yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I figured you would have at least brought a few people along for appearances' sake. It appears I underestimated just how confidential the mission was.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Shouldn't you have gotten used to confidential missions by now? That's just how the courts operate.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: So... what gift must the loser give? Tea?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: He already has tons of tea in his office. I'm thinking about a set of legal codices.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: That wouldn't happen to be a dig at my lack of legal awareness, would it...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Well, I'm sure His Grace doesn't consider the Fortress to be outside the law.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I was under the impression the residents of a place like this would be uninterested in the legal codices...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Uh, that was obviously a joke.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Anyway, you've still got some unfinished business to attend to in the overworld, correct?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: No need to stay here if you have a pressing matter. We all know you can't leave Palais Mermonia for long.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: ...Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: (I hope everything went smoothly with the Fatui Harbinger.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Neuvillette! Why are you here?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, I need you to head to the opera house immediately.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Furina will soon be meeting with The Knave there. You must protect Furina and make sure she doesn't spend too much time alone with her.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Okay, you can explain everything else to me later!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Will do. You have my sincerest gratitude.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, there are a ton of Fatui and Palais Mermonia people over there! The Knave is probably here already... We need to hurry!

dialogues.speaker: Receptionist
dialogues.text: #Are you two {NICKNAME} and Paimon? Monsieur Neuvillette has left instructions. Please follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Receptionist
dialogues.text: Though I'm sure he's already explained, this should be a mostly cordial conversation unlikely to give rise to violence, but it would be most appreciated if you could protect Lady Furina to the best of your abilities.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I will do my best.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Oh, so you two are the honored guests Miss Furina mentioned.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Of course, of course! How could they not attend a meeting such as this? I must always have two or more guests at my dessert table, otherwise the occasion would be too lonely and unbecoming of my station.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: #It is my pleasure to make your acquaintance, {NICKNAME}, I have heard much of your accomplishments. I am The Knave, one of the eleven Fatui Harbingers.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So this is The Knave... the head of the House of the Hearth, and the Lyney siblings' "Father." She certainly does not seem easy to deal with.)

choices.text: Greetings.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I've already prepared seats for you. Come, sit beside me.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Perhaps you two are unaware of how Miss Furina and I do things. You see, we actually recently agreed to get together for tea when we had the time.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: See this? This is a limited type of confectionery that Miss Furina simply adores. There are only sixteen slices sold every day. Here, why don't you and Paimon have a taste?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (She seems friendly enough, but that can't be all there is to her... The Knave is a force to be reckoned with. I should be very cautious around her.)

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, what do you think of this cake?

choices.text: It's pretty good.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: That's good to hear. So what Childe said was on the mark after all... you do share a taste in desserts with Furina and I.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Wait, Childe should have no reason to have said something like that.)

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: I wonder how he's doing nowadays. You must have heard, right? He's suddenly gone missing. I'm really worried about his safety, you know. Here's to hoping that he's an excellent swimmer.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I have faith in his abilities.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Uh... Since we're talking about him, I feel like I should add something. His martial prowess really looked... certainly pretty impressive, yeah!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Furina looks quite nervous... There must be some kind of bad blood between her and The Knave.)

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Oh, so you're also familiar with his aptitude for fighting, Miss Furina? Ah, right, I almost forgot. Childe was subdued by Iudex Neuvillette right in front of you.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Against ordinary people, my colleague would never be on the back foot, but alas, he just never imagined he'd run into such a person... Hmm... I must express my admiration for Monsieur Neuvillette.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I managed to find a few leads on his whereabouts.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Hmm. Coming from you, that's not surprising at all.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Eh? But... I thought you would be happier to hear the news...?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Of course, but it's still a bit of a shame. You see, I would have been far happier had I received this news somewhat earlier. As you well know, a long time has passed since Childe disappeared.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Well, in any case, there's no need to worry! We know for sure that Childe is still alive!

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Oh? And just how do you know that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Because... Because we found evidence that proved he left the Fortress of Meropide!

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: And where did he go after leaving the Fortress?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Oh no... Paimon's statement just left us wide open...)

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: The Fortress of Meropide lies deep beneath the waves. Unless he pranced right out of the main gate, he must have had to swim for it. Do you have any proof that he surfaced safely?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...We do not.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But there was also no evidence that he's been injured or killed.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Ah, that is good news at least. His sister Tonia sent a letter to Fontaine not too long ago. Since he was unfortunately unavailable, I picked it up on his behalf.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Do you have any idea how he usually writes back to his family? "Dear Tonia, your letter made me feel like we were still enjoying our time in Snezhnaya together. I'm currently admiring the scenery on the streets in front of the opera house..." Is it something like that?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (She's turning up the pressure, I'm not sure if I'll be able to convince her... But I can at least try to distract her from Furina.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That sounds good to me, yes.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: All letters tend to follow the same few formats anyway, right? As long as the contents are accurate, it doesn't matter so much how it's written, or how it's worded...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hold on! The water in the teacup is shaking...?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: I suppose this is also a sign of things to come, Miss Furina.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Huh? Ah, I don't quite understand what you're trying to say...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: —Have we entered into the next stage of the prophecy?

choices.text: It's quite tasty, and I think Paimon agrees too.
Pleasure to meet you, too.

talks.objective: Continue taking part in the tea party

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: *sigh* I must say, we've spent long enough playing house.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Miss Furina. As the Hydro Archon, I am sure you understand the exact meaning of the phenomenon we just witnessed. Or should I say, that's what I originally thought, but looking at your expression... was I wrong, and you haven't a clue?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: ...What are you trying to say?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: At this point, I don't think there's any more need to speak as diplomatic representatives. Allow me to speak to you now as just a Fontainian: You know the prophecy by heart, and also that every part of it is being proven true.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Yet here you are relaxing, drinking tea and eating desserts as if it's all nothing more than a few stray bugs in your garden. Do you really think that's acceptable?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: The prophecy's hanging above our necks like a guillotine. Every faction is looking for a way to either avert the disaster or save their own. Even the orphans of the House of the Hearth have devoted everything to saving their homeland.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: But you? It beggars belief just how nonchalant and carefree you have been. From the very beginning, you, the god Focalors... You have utterly failed to take action.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: You're wrong... I've never ignored the prophecy, nor have I just been passing the time in self-indulgence. Retract your accusation, and stop doubting the wisdom of the gods with such absurd conjectures!

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: I am not alone in my doubts, you know. All the children of Fontaine may be harboring the exact same thoughts right now.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: O great Hydro Archon, how are you going to save them? Save us? How are the people you've sworn to protect supposed to survive in a land that will soon disappear beneath the waves?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I have my ways, and I've been working on them for all this time... Even if you look down upon me, you have no right to judge me!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Fontaine will be saved. Even... Even if I still cannot see the true future right now, as long as I continue on as I am, I will be able to hold my head up high!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Furina's not acting like her usual self. She's actually seriously refuting The Knave's accusations... She means what she says. She's not putting on a front.)

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Then I ask you, Miss Furina, just what have you been working on? Where can we see it, and what is it doing to help?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...So was that all a lie? Or can she really not tell us? She was so full of conviction and confidence just now, but now she's deflated like a popped balloon.)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: ...My machinations are just like the prophecy itself — they will only reveal themselves at the fated time. It is just that beings like yourselves are unable to perceive them as of yet.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: I see. As a god, the proof of your labor always lies beyond prying mortal eyes.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Allow me to be so bold as to ask another way. Would it be possible for you to tell us the parts of your plan that are not confidential? Such as... your emergency response plan for the impending disaster.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Uh... An emergency response plan...?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Ah, that look in your eyes... Have you not even prepared one of those?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: The... The emergency response plan is also strictly confidential.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Then allow me to jog your memory. Miss Furina, what is the purpose of your Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: And what do you plan to do with the massive amounts of Indemnitium that it has accumulated over the years?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Th—The Oratrice? It... It's just like it appears to be...

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Hmph, so you also have no idea? If I'm not mistaken, someone's using it to prepare for something. But unfortunately, it would seem that someone is not you, Miss Furina.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: I first caught wind of this when Lyney tried to investigate the Oratrice in the opera house. You see, even just getting close to the core contaminated him with an extremely large amount of Indemnitium.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: But if even that had nothing to do with you... Then what could you possibly be working on, O great Hydro Archon?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Oh, right, I almost forgot. Iudex Neuvillette is not at the tea party with us today. Miss Furina, I suppose you must have ordered him away to take care of some troublesome business.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Ah, yeah, yes, that's exactly right! Please keep it a secret for me.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Of course I will. Although I must say, Miss Furina, you seem quite insecure without the Iudex by your side.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Very well, let's stop that conversation here. There are still a few slices of cake left, so please help yourselves, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (These aren't topics I can speak about... I don't even know what Neuvillette's task was.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If I had to guess, he probably went down to deal with the surging Primordial Sea... But can he really deal with it all by himself?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (And is Furina being truthful or not?)

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, I heard that you were recently commissioned to handle a few matters on behalf of the Iudex. Why don't you take an extra slice of cake? Those who work hard deserve gratitude and praise.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: You too, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Er... Thank you, Paimon will take you up on that offer...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The Knave proceeds to change the topic and brings up a number of less significant matters. While the atmosphere gradually becomes more relaxed, the somber feeling from the prior conversation remains in everyone's hearts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! Paimon's super full. That cake was great!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Mhm-mmm, if it's on my tea table, it must be of the highest quality. Ah, yes, and we must thank The Knave for bringing these over as well.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: You're welcome. I'm sure the cake also felt greatly honored to be featured at Miss Furina's table. And I was merely catering to Miss Furina's tastes, seeking a chance to chat over tea.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: It is getting late. Why don't we call it a day? There are still a few matters that I need to take care of, so I must take my leave now.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Very well, we'll end it here.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: #Mind seeing me off, {NICKNAME}? We could use the opportunity to discuss Childe before I must be on my way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Of course.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's coming, too!

talks.objective: Follow The Knave to the exit

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: I'm glad that you were willing to come with me. Of course, Childe was just an excuse. I have no interest in your dealings with him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's what Paimon thought!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you want to say?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: You lent your aid to the children of the House of the Hearth. As their "Father," I would like to express my gratitude.

choices.text: ...There's no need.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Was there nothing else you wanted to say?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: That was all. Formal topics should be discussed in formal settings, and informal topics in informal settings.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: I know you just returned from the Fortress of Meropide. Relax, I have no intention of trying to get anything out of you. Lyney, Lynette and Freminet are still there, and I trust their judgment and abilities.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They've all been working very hard, and have always done all they can to fight back against anyone who tried to stop them! Especially Lyney...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: You mean Wriothesley. He's a tricky one to deal with. It's unfortunate that Lyney's so eager to prove himself that he can't learn to rely on others... including me.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: By the way, and you can just consider this a bit of idle gossip, but what's your impression of Furina?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: You are outside of our disputes, and the freest person in all of Fontaine, able to move around most easily. Allow me to share my perspective with you.

response.speaker: Fatui Sergeant
response.text: ...And that's everything that happened during the trial. Master Childe was declared guilty, and immediately transported to the Fortress of Meropide.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Didn't he say he was coming here on vacation? Does he not feel an ounce of shame for all the trouble he has caused?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Forget it. He did give us an opportunity.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: I will be meeting someone shortly.

response.speaker: Fatui Sergeant
response.text: Do you require help with any preparations?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: No need. I will take care of it myself.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: (I need to meet with Furina, the Hydro Archon. She is at the heart of Fontaine, but what's fascinating about her is that, she often seems more like a celebrity than a working Archon.)

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Oh? Come over here, you little critter you!

response.speaker: Stray Cat
response.text: Mrrow!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: You dare to run from me? Stop right this instant!

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: (My goal is just to discover the location of the Gnosis, but I didn't expect the chance to approach Furina to be handed to me on a silver platter. This is so easy, it's actually making me a bit suspicious...)

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: (Anything left unguarded is usually just bait. But no one will blame someone for taking the bait. After all, from the moment it was attached to the hook, the bait is meant to be sacrificed.)

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Waaaaaah!

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: (It's just as I guessed in the second before I struck. The Hydro Gnosis is not currently held by the Archon...)

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: (In fact, this "archon" doesn't seem like a god at all... And I sense that she's under some kind of curse...)

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Who are you? A—And wh—what are you trying to do? Please don't kill me, I'm begging you, please...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: (The fear in her pupils is genuine, so perhaps she is not bait after all. Either way, targeting her has lost all meaning.)

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: (I left the scene with ease. Nobody came looking for me, and nobody could serve as a witness to my near-assassination of Focalors. I suspect even Furina dares not mention this incident to anyone.)

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: (Not long after, my informants confirmed what I had guessed: After returning to her quarters, Furina quietly cried alone. She was so scared that she could not sleep that night, nor could she even bring herself to eat her cake.)

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: (There's no doubt that there's something wrong with her. I began to entertain the possibility that she is not the true Hydro Archon — perhaps Iudex Neuvillette is actually the genuine article.)

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: (I have to find the Gnosis. If the Neuvillette hypothesis is correct, he is probably in possession of it. Alternatively, it might have been hidden in a place that's hard for ordinary people to access.)

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Yes, "Father"!

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: My dear children. Please speak.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: News from the Fortress of Meropide. Master... Master Childe has gone missing. On top of that, the contacts and guards we bribed at the Fortress have all gone quiet as well...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: ...Probably the handiwork of that Wriothesley.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: I'm afraid so.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: This is a good opportunity. The value of a Harbinger is much higher than most would imagine. We now have an excuse to exert diplomatic pressure on the Fontaine authorities.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Set up a meeting for me. I would like to meet the Hydro Archon and Iudex Neuvillette.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Oh, and I have an additional mission for you three.

response.speaker: Together
response.text: Yes, "Father"!

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: (Tartaglia's disappearance was not a part of my plan, but I can use it to make a breakthrough. With this as my excuse, I can ask for an official audience, and continue my investigation of Furina and Iudex Neuvillette.)

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: (The initiative belongs to the House of the Hearth. My wish to investigate the Fortress of Meropide will be a front. Lyney and his group will be responsible for the actual intelligence-gathering.)

choices.text: ...I didn't think that's what you wanted to talk about.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Do I look like an irresponsible "Father" to you? Hehe, the House of the Hearth is very important to me. You should know that I care deeply about my children.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: You should know the rest. Lyney's group is quite close to you, so they wouldn't have hidden anything from you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y—You attacked the Hydro Archon?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: It wouldn't mean anything even if you shouted it from the rooftops. After all, even Furina herself is still pretending that nothing of that sort ever happened.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, alright then...

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: I've now had two chances to enjoy tea with Furina. I have to say, the leadership of Fontaine is even more inscrutable than I had imagined. I once surmised that Iudex Neuvillette must be the Hydro Archon, but now, that doesn't seem right to me either.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How did you come to that conclusion?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: I am a servant of Her Majesty the Tsaritsa. Over my years of service, I've learned how a real Archon conducts and carries themselves. Whether Iudex Neuvillette or Furina, neither fits the bill. It's hard to imagine either of them as the Archon.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Of course, that is all just how I feel. Gut feelings often do not require justification.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: It is, however, quite amusing to me that after all my years working in intelligence gathering, I've come to realize I am at a complete loss regarding the identity of the god of the land of my birth.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Don't you think Fontaine is quite intriguing? A catastrophe looms, yet many secrets have yet to rise to the surface. It looks like Fontainians will have no choice but to save themselves.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Ultimately, though, one must survive in order to do anything else. Should the need arise, I would be happy to cooperate with you.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: You don't need to commit to anything right now, of course. I have a feeling that the situation will continue to evolve. And as your name is often connected with noble deeds, I'm sure we will work together someday.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Neuvillette?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: He certainly returned quickly. You must want to catch up with each other, so I'll leave you to him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Neuvillette, is it over?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: For now, yes, but this issue will prove quite thorny in the long term. I am concerned that sooner or later, the prophesized events will occur...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Thank you for protecting Furina.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: May we ask what happened down there?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Mmm... To put it simply, I used my power to force back the Primordial Sea and re-seal the sluice gate.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: As for what happened on our side...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You recount the happenings of the tea party to Neuvillette...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: ...So, as expected, The Knave has turned up the pressure on Furina. She's trying to feel her out, though I'm still unsure as to her motives.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can I ask you some questions?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Permission granted.

choices.text: You have enough power to force back the Primordial Sea...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, it can't be that you're the real Hydro Archon, right? But that's just a speculation on our part, though...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You can't tell us? Then... Then that's okay, we can talk about something else, we won't try to force you... Hahaha, you guys in Fontaine are super strange...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: If by the phrase "you guys" you are referring to Furina and I, then although I'm not sure just what you are trying to imply, I must clarify that I do not share her positions on a multitude of topics.

choices.text: What did you sense in the Fortress of Meropide?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I believe so. The Fortress has a long and complex history. It has seen much grief and suffering.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: ...And now, another catastrophe will soon be upon us. I mourn this turn of events.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Why is it raining all of a sudden?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The clear skies suddenly filled with dark clouds. The rain became heavier, light rain soon growing to a downpour.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (And just moments before, Neuvillette has just mentioned his sense of grief.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Thinking back to that legend, and what Freminet said... "It's said that a Dragon of Water once resided in Fontaine. Every time it weeps, the skies will cloud up and pour out rain.")

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait, Neuvillette, you can't be...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: ...You may be closer to the truth than you think.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, and what are you thinking?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...He's the Dragon Sovereign of Water.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Dragon of... Huh wha!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...HUUUUUUUUUHHHH???

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Please do not be so surprised...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: ...Furina?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...villette! Neuvillette! Are you listening?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Ah, my apologies.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We were just guessing randomly... We didn't guess right, did we? You're not actually the Dragon Sovereign of Water, right? Well, if you don't want to confirm or deny...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: You guessed correctly. I sincerely hope you'll be able to keep this a secret for me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah... right! Of course! We'll definitely help you keep it a secret!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's still something Paimon wants to ask you, though...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Please go ahead.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, if you are the Dragon Sovereign of Water, and you were able to force back the Primordial Sea from the Fortress...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then since Fontaine's prophecy is all about seawater, couldn't you just use your power to solve the crisis?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: None of the currently living dragon sovereigns in the world, myself included, possess our full dragonhood.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: They say that when the First Usurper arrived on Teyvat, they seized a part of the dragons' power. Today, that stolen power is the basis of the Archons' Authorities.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There are seven elemental Archons, and seven matching Dragon Sovereigns...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: The Dragon Sovereign of Water who lived through that era perished a long time ago. As their successor, I know far less of that part of our ancient history.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: In any case, I believe I will not be able to do much unless the Archon disappears and returns their elemental Authority to me.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Given the status quo, however, I would recommend finding another way to deal with the prophecy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... So even you can't solve it...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I still have some urgent matters to attend to at my office. If you have any more questions regarding ancient history, you are welcome to discuss them with me at a later time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, please go right ahead! There's a place that Paimon wants to go, too. Traveler, why don't we pay another visit to the Fortress of Meropide? Paimon is a little worried...

choices.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll see you another time!

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Take care.

choices.text: See you later, Neuvillette.
Did you manage to protect those that needed to be defended?
Does this mean you have some deeper connection with the Hydro Archon?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: I feel like... I should try to become someone more capable of helping.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: You're incredibly helpful. Lyney thinks so too.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Yeah. You two are always telling me not to push myself, but aren't you just like that as well?

dialogues.speaker: Guard
dialogues.text: Halt! Where are you going?

dialogues.speaker: Guard
dialogues.text: His Grace has already given the order to evacuate. Please leave the area in an orderly fashion, and watch your step!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (No, I have to go to the forbidden zone right away to check on the situation there.)

dialogues.speaker: Guard
dialogues.text: His Grace has asked everyone to evacuate outwards as quickly as possible. You should get a move on.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: ...The tea party turned out to be even more difficult than I'd imagined...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Huh? Ah... Ahem! Why are you looking at me like that? Is something the matter? If there's nothing urgent, then I shall be retiring for now.

dialogues.speaker: Prison Broadcast
dialogues.text: Attention! Please evacuate upwards and outwards, upwards and outwards! If you're already at the topmost layer, then try to move as far outwards as possible!
